question: Does actual PPO optimize K1 purchases using GP mean, SD, incumbent, and normal CDF/density features?
features: Five fixed input slots: mu, sigma, incumbent, Phi(z), phi(z), with z=(mu-incumbent)/max(sigma,1e-12). The matched three-input policy masks the last two channels. Same scalar encoder, singleton subset blocks, remaining-pool summaries, and count features as previous feature experiments.
policy: Categorical distribution over unmeasured compounds during training; deterministic highest-score choice for primary held-out evaluation. No MiniMol coordinates, delta summaries, explicit EI or weighted EI summands are model inputs.
starts: Two separate initializations per feature set: GP-mean policy (zero residual actor, mean coefficient2), or600-step EI-imitation pretraining. EI imitation is used only for initialization; pure PPO follows. Starting policies are evaluated separately for matched before/after comparisons.
reinforcement_learning: Full on-policy trajectories. A selected molecule is revealed, the frozen GP posterior conditions on its measured outcome, and the policy acts again. Reward is minus1 per purchase, including the successful purchase; episode terminates at a true optimum. Initial hit costs0. Ties qualify. No optimum-membership or property-regression loss during PPO.
returns: Undiscounted Monte Carlo return = negative number of purchases remaining in that sampled episode (gamma1). Advantage = return minus pre-update critic value, standardized across the rollout batch with scale floor1. No truncation/bootstrap at episode ends.
optimizer: Clipped PPO likelihood-ratio surrogate, entropy bonus, separate critic with squared return error. Critic receives the same permitted inputs and its gradients cannot update actor parameters. Adam, gradient norm clipping1, minibatches64,2 or3 epochs per rollout batch. No EI imitation, classification, regression-to-property, or auxiliary pair losses in PPO updates.
sampling: Eight complete episodes per PPO update. Episode starts sample the worse half of the pool. Training draws from >=15 pools with probability0.5, otherwise all eligible training pools. Independent RNG streams for pool/start sampling and optimizer minibatch order. Only current-policy actions generate PPO training transitions.
data: Frozen neural-mean/conventional-kernel GP; unchanged predictor/selector role split and linked-series outer folds. Six endpoints, five folds, three final model seeds, four common held-out initial hits. Starting-hit relative utility and existing endpoint scaling unchanged.
selection: Four configurations per feature/initialization arm:80 PPO updates in screening; two finalists400 updates; winner repeated at seeds29/47. Select among PPO steps40/80 in screening and100/200/400 in refinement. Initial checkpoint is NOT eligible to be reported as PPO. Select on validation normalized top1 purchases, mixed all pools and >=15 pools.12 screen/32 refine validation pools, one common start.
evaluation: Primary deterministic purchases to any top1/2/3/4 on all4,625 held-out pools; >=15 pools primary. Report initial and updated policies separately. Additional stochastic diagnostic uses two sampled trajectories from the first common hit per pool per model seed. Shared-context EI agreement is diagnostic only.
statistics: Paired linked-group bootstrap after averaging hits/seeds. Six pooled >=15 top1 primary comparisons: five-input PPO vs three-input PPO within each initialization; five-input PPO vs analytic EI within each initialization; five-input PPO vs its own start within each initialization. Holm adjustment over6 comparisons. Exploratory development-fold evaluation.
source: PPO clipped-surrogate approach follows Schulman et al., Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms (https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.06347). Actor feature architecture and frozen molecular GP inherited from this project.
